task.title: Set up two-factor authentication (2FA) for your individual Red Hat account
task.shortdesc: To secure your individual Red Hat user account when organization-wide two-factor authentication is not required, you will need to enable 2FA and set up an authenticator app on your smartphone or other device.

ul.li: Ensure you are using a registered Red Hat user account.
Ensure you have a smartphone or other device with the Google Authenticator app or the FreeOTP app installed.

prereq.note: Google Authenticator and FreeOTP Authenticator are the only supported token generators for providing two-factor authentication one-time codes. Hardware tokens, SMS (text-message) tokens, and other apps are not supported. You can install these apps on your smartphone or other compatible Android or iOS device.

If your company policy requires two-factor authentication to access your Red Hat account and you have not yet enabled two-factor authentication, you will see the instructions to enable two-factor authentication immediately after you log in.

step.cmd: Log in to your Red Hat user account on any Red Hat site, such as Red Hat Customer Portal.
Click your user avatar in the upper right corner of the panel.

substep.cmd: Click Account details. A page opens where you can edit your account information.
If you log in through Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, click My profile under your user avatar to edit your account information.

stepresult.p: A page opens where you can review your account information.
stepresult.note: Depending on which login portal you use, a different icon may appear.

step.cmd: On the Login & password page click Manage two-factor authentication. The Signing in page opens.
On the Signing in page, click Set up authenticator application. You must log in again to verify your account before the Enable two-factor authentication page opens.
Open the authenticator app on your smart phone and select the option to add a token. You can use one of these methods to add a token for the Red Hat two-factor authentication.

substep.cmd: Use the authenticator app to scan the QR code that opens on the two-factor authentication page.
Alternatively, you can click Unable to scan? Enter the key instead which displays a 32-character key string that you must enter into your authenticator app.

step.cmd: After you scan the QR code (or enter the key string), the authenticator app creates an initial one-time 6-digit code. Enter this code into the One-time code field.
You can enter an optional name in the Device name field. This name can remind you which of your mobile devices has the authenticator app for this login.
Click Enable to complete setting up two-factor authentication.

note.p: While you update your signing in options, you might be asked to log in again. This is a normal action and is provided to increase account security.

result.p: The Signing In page opens when the authenticator app was set up and any optional name you gave to the app.
